neighbours.label: best guess: demonstrative ' that' / ' such' standing right after a preposition or comparison word (for that night, about that of, like that, in such a way)
fire: We rented a cabin for that weekend and brought all the food.
The island has an area about that of a large farm.
The array must have a shape like that given in the table.
They agreed to meet on that morning before the shops opened.
The old mill used a wheel about that size to grind corn.
She kept a diary during that winter and wrote in it daily.
The valves are fitted in such a way that no water escapes.
He had never seen a storm like that before in his life.
quiet: We rented a cabin so that everyone could bring some food.
The island that we visited was as large as a farm.
She said that the array must have a different shape.
They agreed that the shops opened too late in the morning.
The old mill used a large wheel to grind corn.
She kept a diary and wrote in it every winter day.
The valves are fitted so tightly that no water escapes.
He had never seen a storm so strong in his life.

notes: Weak in probes: 'about that of' 0.39, 'like that shown' 0.23, 'for that night' 0.19, but 'similar to that of' 0.02 and a short 'in such a way' sentence 0.02, although ' such a way' leads the top examples. The pole probably needs something this label does not name. Near misses use complementizer or relative 'that'.
